summary:
EarthScope AI is a browser-based planetary research laboratory developed by the RoboKids team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project directly addresses the Earth System Trend Detective challenge by integrating 24 years of public data from NASA satellite missions and reanalysis models (2001–2024), covering key variables such as rainfall, vegetation (EVI), land surface temperature, air temperature, and relative humidity. 
The platform features an interactive 3D terrestrial globe—which can also be explored in immersive virtual and mixed reality (VR/MR) environments via WebXR—allowing anyone to compare years using sliding curtain tools, track live natural events via EONET, and examine experimental neural network projections out to 2030. It also incorporates a multimodal AI assistant capable of responding via voice or text using real backend scientific tools.
To resolve the complexity of environmental analysis, EarthScope AI lets users select points or custom-drawn polygons anywhere on Earth. The system calculates exact rates of change using Sen's slope and rigorously evaluates whether trends are statistically significant (p<0.05) by applying seasonal Mann-Kendall tests with autocorrelation correction, alongside robustness checks against recent extreme years. Its importance lies in democratizing access to Earth observation data, helping researchers, students, and citizens distinguish true climate change signals from natural variability with scientific honesty.
details:
EarthScope AI is a browser-based planetary research laboratory built by the RoboKids team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Integrating your team's core design pillars with the technical specifications of the platform, here is a detailed breakdown of the project:

 1. What It Does and How It Works

EarthScope AI functions on a decoupled client-server architecture where the web interface handles visualization while the backend performs all scientific calculations.

  • Data Processing & Visualization: It ingests 24 years of real NASA satellite and reanalysis data (2001–2024) across five key variables—rainfall (GPM IMERG), vegetation (MODIS EVI), land surface temperature (MODIS), air temperature (MERRA-2), and relative humidity (MERRA-2)—standardized onto a global 0.5°
     grid.
  • Interactive Exploration: Users can click any point or draw custom polygons anywhere on the 3D globe to inspect time-series charts, use a sliding curtain comparator to contrast two different years, and view live natural events (wildfires, storms, volcanoes) via NASA EONET.
  • Real-Time Orbital Tracking: The platform calculates and renders the real-time positions and trajectories of 19 satellites in space using CelesTrak TLE orbits and the SGP4 model, color-coding them by their specific role in data collection or calibration.
  • Statistical Engine & AI: For any selected region, the backend calculates Sen's slope to measure exact rates of change per decade and runs seasonal Mann-Kendall tests (p<0.05) with Hirsch-Slack autocorrelation correction alongside robustness checks to filter out natural noise. It also includes an experimental U-Net neural network ensemble projecting anomalies out to 2030 and a conversational AI assistant that operates via text and voice to move the globe and run analyses.

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Accessible Research for All Ages & Skill Levels: Designed with an intuitive, step-by-step interface, interactive visual/auditory controls, and guided educational stories (such as the Central Amazon case study), the platform serves everyone from curious beginners and students to professional researchers.
  • Multilingual & Inclusive: Featuring a bilingual interface (English and Spanish) and a multilingual voice interaction, it removes language and technical barriers.
  • Actionable Scientific Output: Beyond visual exploration, users can uncover environmental patterns, study natural phenomena, and export processed datasets, trend maps, and series (such as PNG images and JSON series) for external research.
  • Intended Impact: The project aims to democratize Earth observation data and foster honest scientific communication—empowering society to distinguish genuine, statistically robust climate trends from normal year-to-year variability without exaggeration.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used

  • Frontend: Built with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS 4. 3D rendering, orbital math, and charts rely on react-globe.gl, three.js, satellite.js, Recharts, Zustand, and Motion. Immersive exploration is enabled via WebXR for virtual and mixed reality (VR/MR) headsets, while voice capabilities use Web Speech and ElevenLabs.
  • Backend & Data Science: Powered by Python 3, FastAPI, and Uvicorn. Data ingestion and numerical processing utilize earthaccess, h5py, pyhdf, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, pymannkendall, and statsmodels.
  • AI & Machine Learning: Experimental climate projections use PyTorch while the tool-calling conversational agent is built with LangChain, Gemini, Claude, and ElevenLabs.

4. Creativity and Key Factors Considered by the Team

  • Creative Integration: Combining a holographic 3D globe, live orbital mechanics, WebXR virtual reality, and a voice-controlled AI agent that physically manipulates the map creates an engaging, multi-sensory research environment.
  • Scientific Honesty & Guardrails: A core design factor was preventing misinterpretation. The team enforced strict visual and textual distinctions between observations (satellite measurements), reanalysis (model reconstructions), experimental projections (2030 AI estimates), and "what-if" scenarios. Furthermore, if a user selects an area lacking sufficient valid data (such as vegetation over an ocean), the system transparently explains the limitation rather than inventing results.
  • Performance & Reproducibility: To ensure smooth browser performance and user privacy, heavy statistical computations were isolated in the backend and datasets were pre-aggregated into lightweight grids. The team also considered statistical fragility, explicitly flagging trends that rely heavily on recent record-breaking years like 2023 and 2024.
